title: Creamy scrambled eggs on toast
summary: Five minutes, three eggs, and very easy to overcook: perfect for a demo.
source: Written for REMY by Claude. No timer: scrambled eggs are judged by eye (3–5 min on low, see cook-times.json). Checked by Matthew on 2026-11-07.
notes: Runny, soft eggs are a personal choice. For anyone vulnerable (pregnant, elderly, very young, unwell), cook until firm: see food-safety.json.
ingredients: Pinch of salt and black pepper
1 slice of bread for toast (plus butter)

steps.instruction: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and beat with a fork until completely smooth. Put the bread in the toaster now.
looks_right: an even yellow colour with no streaks of white
a few small bubbles on top
looks_wrong: bits of shell in the bowl (scoop them out with a bigger piece of shell)
steps.done_when: The eggs are smooth and evenly yellow.

steps.instruction: Melt the butter in the non-stick pan on LOW heat. Patience is the whole trick.
looks_right: butter melting slowly with a light foam
looks_wrong: butter browning or sizzling hard (heat too high: take it off for a moment)
steps.done_when: The butter has melted and is gently foaming.

steps.instruction: Pour in the eggs. Stir slowly and constantly with the spatula, sweeping from the edges to the middle.
looks_right: eggs still glossy and a little wet
looks_wrong: eggs setting instantly around the edges (too hot: lift the pan off the heat)
steps.done_when: Soft curds have formed, but they still look a bit wet and shiny.

steps.instruction: Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly underdone, because they keep cooking. Season with pepper and stir in the chives.
looks_wrong: water seeping out of the eggs (overcooked)
steps.done_when: The pan is off the heat and the eggs are creamy and glossy.

steps.instruction: Butter the toast and pile the eggs on top straight away.
looks_right: eggs sitting soft on the toast
looks_wrong: eggs left in the hot pan while the toast is buttered (they go dry)
